advisory: Computed, not celebrated. Every date here is derived from the arithmetic in guidance/liturgy/calendar-computation.md and is a finding aid only. The competent General, territorial, diocesan, religious, parish and church calendar, the approved books and the competent annual Ordo control an actual celebration. Verify against a dated official witness before relying on any date, and never cite this file as an occurrence witness.
days_note: A civil date absent from `days` carries no mass in this calendar's index: the day is computed, and no formulary for it has been written. A date present carries one entry per candidate, in the order temporal-then-fixed-date; more than one entry means the day is unranked, in the sense of `precedence` above. `rule` indexes `rules`, which says how the date was derived; `territorial`, when present, names the option the candidate holds under and is absent when it holds under both. A candidate's `key` is a mass in this calendar's own propers structure, where its title and text live; the season and, in Ordinary Time, the week of any date are read from the spans in `liturgical_years`.
ferial_formulary_note: `ferial_formulary` answers a different question from `days`, for the same dates. `days` says which masses a date carries as celebrations. This says which Mass a feria of that date takes when it has none of its own: RGMR 299 gives a proper Mass to the ferias of Lent and Passiontide and to the six Ember Days of Advent and September, and appoints the Mass of the preceding Sunday on every other feria unless the rubrics provide otherwise. The entry is a reference and never a copy: `key` names a mass in this calendar's own propers structure, exactly as a `days` entry does, and `rule` indexes the same `rules` list. Whether the day actually is a feria is not decided here and never was: a date carrying a feast carries its ferial formulary too, unused, because precedence belongs to structure/rubrics/<calendar>.json and this layer states no ranking. A date is absent where the season gives the feria a Mass of its own or no rubric in this calendar appoints a formulary the index carries. A rubric that explicitly provides otherwise may name a different formulary than the preceding Sunday's. Every borrowing emitted here carries the WHOLE formulary, because RGMR 299 gives the feria the Mass of the preceding Sunday and a Mass is all of it. A calendar whose rubric lends less than a whole Mass may not use this block unscoped; see `scope` in the block below, which nothing emits yet.

precedence.note: No general table of precedence is stated in guidance/liturgy/calendar-computation.md, so a date carrying more than one candidate lists them all unranked, temporal candidates before fixed-date ones. The `rank` a candidate carries is the rank its own calendar prints, not a computed ordering, and it does not resolve the day. The competent Ordo decides which mass is said. `appointed` is the one exception, and it states no precedence either: a commemoration is not a rival mass but a text said within the mass of the day, so setting the commemorations aside reads what the index records rather than ordering what it does not. Where more than one mass remains after that, `appointed` is null.

territorial.note: Universal Norms 7 assigns these celebrations to a Sunday only where the competent authority has actually so decided. Both forms are emitted; a candidate tagged with one option holds only under that option, and an untagged candidate holds under both. This file does not know which option applies in any place, and a transfer is never inferred from arithmetic.
